On the night of gengyin in the twelfth month of the second year of Yuanguang, Emperor Xuanzong fell gravely ill. 英王 is Prince Ying, not Jing, and 中宮 at the dying emperor's bedside is the empress, not an empress dowager.

He was bright and sharp, unrestrained by convention, broadly learned and skilled in discussion, adept at documents, and wrote with a clear, beautiful hand in the manner of the Wei-Jin calligraphers.

The original Jin period is ambiguous with the Jin house of this history; the proposal's parenthetical graph is not allowed in the English field. Wei-Jin names the calligraphic tradition meant by the source.
Bright and sharp, unrestrained by convention, broadly learned and skilled at discussion, adept at documents, writing clear and beautiful with Jin-ren style.
Bright and sharp, unrestrained by convention, broadly learned and skilled at discussion, adept at documents, writing clear and beautiful in the style of the Wei-Jin masters.
Jin-ren style leaves the two Jin dynasties confused, and the proposed English still inserts a Chinese graph. Wei-Jin is the intended calligraphic manner.

In the twelfth month he acted as commander-in-chief of the Shandong West and East circuits, and also held the posts of military commissioner of the Military Pacification Army and observation commissioner within Xuzhou.

In the twelfth month he conducted the affairs of the commander-in-chief of the Shandong West Circuit, and also held the posts of military commissioner of the Wuning Army and observation commissioner within Xuzhou.
山東西路 is the West Shandong circuit, not west and east circuits; 武甯軍 is the Wuning Army, not Military Pacification Army.
Several hundred Song horsemen came out to resist. Yawuta feigned a northward retreat, sprang an ambush, and beheaded two hundred men.
Several hundred Song horsemen came out to resist. Yawuta feigned defeat, sprang an ambush, and beheaded two hundred men.
佯北 is a feigned defeat (敗北), not a retreat northward.
Song men came out with several hundred horsemen to resist; Yawuta commanded troops to feign retreat north, sprang ambush and struck them, beheading two hundred.
Song men came out with several hundred horsemen to resist; Yawuta commanded troops to feign defeat, sprang an ambush and struck them, beheading two hundred.
The literal feign retreat north makes the same 北-as-north error.
Shi Qing stood on the wall directing the defense. A shot struck Yawuta in the eye, and Shi Qing then withdrew his force south in flight.
Shi Qing stood on the wall directing the defense. A shot struck him in the eye, and he then withdrew his force south in flight.
射中其目 follows 時青乘城指麾; 其 and the ensuing 南奔 refer to Shi Qing, not Yawuta.
Shi Qing stood on the wall commanding; a shot struck Yawuta in the eye, whereupon Shi Qing withdrew his force south in flight.
Shi Qing stood on the wall commanding; a shot struck his eye, whereupon he withdrew his force south in flight.
The literal field invents Yawuta as the patient of 其目 against the same Chinese referent.

After Liuge was killed the people still resisted. As Yawuta was pressing the assault, Song chief Liu Bin, superintendent Huang Wen, and others sent the heads of the rebels Luan Yanjun, Qi Yi, and Wanyan Qige, and displayed the head of superintendent Jinshan Bada, dispatching their adjutants Ma Jun and Wu Gui to present them.

After Liuge was killed the people still resisted. As Yawuta was pressing the assault, Song chief Liu Bin, superintendent Huang Wen, and others bound the ringleaders Yan Jun, Qi Yi, and Wanyan Qige, and displayed the head of superintendent Jinshan Bada, dispatching their adjutants Ma Jun and Wu Gui to present them.
顏俊 is Yan Jun; 縛首亂 means they bound the ringleaders, while only 梟……首 beheads Jinshan Bada. Luan Yanjun is a ghost name from 亂.

After Liuge was killed the masses still resisted; as he was pressing the assault, Song chief Liu Bin, superintendent Huang Wen, and others bound the heads of the rebels Luan Yanjun, Qi Yi, Wanyan Qige, and displayed the head of superintendent Jinshan Bada, sending their adjutants Ma Jun and Wu Gui to present them.

After Liuge was killed the masses still resisted; as he was pressing the assault, Song chief Liu Bin, superintendent Huang Wen, and others bound the ringleader rebels Yan Jun, Qi Yi, and Wanyan Qige, and displayed the head of superintendent Jinshan Bada, sending their adjutants Ma Jun and Wu Gui to present them.
The literal bound the heads of the rebels Luan Yanjun repeats the 首亂/顏俊 misread; ringleader Yan Jun is correct.
Prince Jing Shouchun said, "For all who serve as generals and commanders, controlling talent should all be like this."
Prince Ying Shouchun said, "For all who serve as generals and commanders, controlling talent should all be like this."
英王守純 is Prince Ying Shouchun, not Prince Jing.
Prince Jing Shouchun said: "For all who serve as generals and commanders, controlling talent should all be like this."
Prince Ying Shouchun said: "For all who serve as generals and commanders, controlling talent should all be like this."
The literal field has the same Jing-for-英 error.

That year, after Great Yuan forces had destroyed the Xia state, they attacked Dexun, Qinzhou, Qingshui, and other cities in Shaanxi, then entered Jingzhao from Fengxiang. Guanzhong was shaken to its core.

That year, after Great Yuan forces had destroyed the Xia state, they attacked Deshun, Qinzhou, Qingshui, and other cities in Shaanxi, then entered Jingzhao from Fengxiang. Guanzhong was shaken to its core.
德順 is Deshun; Dexun is a mistranscription.
That year, after Great Yuan forces had destroyed Xia, they attacked Dexun, Qinzhou, Qingshui, and other cities in Shaanxi, then entered Jingzhao from Fengxiang; Guanzhong shook greatly.
That year, after Great Yuan forces had destroyed Xia, they attacked Deshun, Qinzhou, Qingshui, and other cities in Shaanxi, then entered Jingzhao from Fengxiang; Guanzhong shook greatly.
The literal field likewise writes Dexun for 德順.

In the twelfth month an edict appointed Yawuta and Vice Censor-in-Chief Pu'a to hold acting signatures at the Bureau of Military Affairs, while imperial clansman Wanyan Eke was to lead troops to relieve Qingyang.

In the twelfth month an edict appointed Yawuta and Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Pu'a to hold acting signatures at the Bureau of Military Affairs, while imperial clansman Wanyan Eke was to lead troops to relieve Qingyang.
副樞 is vice-commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, not Vice Censor-in-Chief.

In the twelfth month an edict appointed Yawuta with Vice Censor-in-Chief Pu'a to hold acting signatures at the Bureau of Military Affairs; imperial clansman Eke was to lead troops to relieve Qingyang.

In the twelfth month an edict appointed Yawuta with Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Pu'a to hold acting signatures at the Bureau of Military Affairs; imperial clansman Eke was to lead troops to relieve Qingyang.
The literal field repeats the censorate misreading of 副樞.
He qualified as jinshi in the first year of Zhiyou.
He qualified as jinshi in the first year of Zhining.
至甯元年 is Zhining 1 (至寧); Zhiyou is not this era name.
He gained his jinshi degree in the first year of Zhiyou.
He gained his jinshi degree in the first year of Zhining.
The literal field makes the same Zhiyou error for 至甯.
He was transferred to right secretariat director, Henan South Circuit director of agriculture, and became Hezhong circuit administrator.
He was transferred to Director of the Right Office, Jingnan Circuit assistant director of agriculture, and became Hezhong Circuit administrator.
京南路 is Jingnan Circuit, not Henan South; 司農丞 is an assistant director of agriculture, not director.
He was transferred to Right Secretariat Director, Henan South Circuit Director of Agriculture, and became Hezhong Circuit Administrator.
He was transferred to Director of the Right Office, Jingnan Circuit Assistant Director of Agriculture, and became Hezhong Circuit Administrator.
Jingnan correctly replaces Henan South, but the proposed literal still renders 司農丞 as Director of Agriculture; 丞 is the assistant post.
